clue.text: Fashionable singing in The Bill

parts.note: something fashionable is said to be in
singing is using the voice

explanation.surface: Someone fashionable sings a part in the long-running British police drama The Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals of 'The Bill' point to the TV police series, but the bill here is a request for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill sent for goods or services rendered is a synonym for a trader's invoice.

clue.text: Raids on new invasions

indicators.note: new tells the solver to make a fresh arrangement of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A report of fresh military raids.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile incursions into territory, which is what invasions are.

clue.text: Unfashionable tourist vacation — one perhaps may start here?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise
U is upper class and so fashionable; being un-U means losing that letter

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A holiday that is a bit naff, though a trip might well begin at this London terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfashionable' removes U (old slang for upper-class) from TOURIST VACATION; 'one' adds I, and 'perhaps' rearranges the result. VICTORIA STATION is a big London rail terminus serving the Channel ports and Gatwick.
explanation.definitionFit: This London terminus is where trains to the coast and Gatwick depart, so many holidays begin there.

clue.text: Latin rule translated as malevolence

indicators.note: translating changes words into another form, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman legal principle rendered into English as spitefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolence is a wish to harm others, the spiteful temper meant by a bad disposition.

clue.text: Supporter of visual art

parts.note: reads like a patron of painting, but means the stand that literally holds a canvas up

explanation.definitionFit: A painter's wooden frame stand holds the canvas upright while the picture is worked on.

clue.text: Last word of body in ego trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of the two words beside it fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A dying man's final words come as a jaunt through his own self-regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges BODY and EGO together into the answer; 'in' just links the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is literally the closing remark said on parting, the last word exchanged.

clue.text: Somehow get pardon for one grooming another's child?

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters reach the answer by an unstated route, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tries to win forgiveness for preparing a child who isn't theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor at baptism takes on guidance of someone else's offspring, preparing them in faith.

clue.text: Vegetable rejected by one in repeated refusal

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole assembled run is read backwards
the single letter goes inside the doubled refusal
repeated says the word for refusal appears twice

parts.note: no is a refusal
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A vegetable is turned down by someone who keeps saying no.
explanation.walkthrough: NO doubled is NONO; I goes inside to make NOINO, and 'rejected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a pungent bulb vegetable used throughout cooking.

clue.text: Ready-sliced loaf?

parts.note: loaf is also a verb meaning to laze, so bread that needs no work to cut suits an idler

explanation.definitionFit: A biblical phrase from Proverbs for food eaten without working for it, here pictured as bread already cut.

clue.text: One who writes a letter to a philosopher

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: An author drafts a letter addressed to a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: A. J. Ayer was a leading 20th-century British philosopher of logical positivism.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who essays something attempts it, and the word also names an author of short prose pieces.

clue.text: Dangerous types said to be safe?

definitions.text: Dangerous types said to be safe?

parts.words: Dangerous types said to be safe?
parts.note: said out loud, the first word could be 'wreckless', meaning causing no wrecks, which would make these hazardous motorists sound perfectly safe

explanation.surface: A paradox: hazardous people somehow described as safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists who take careless risks on the road are the dangerous types meant, while the spoken pun suggests vehicle operators with no crashes.

clue.text: Precious metal, or a fraction of a shekel

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, a precious metal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between gold-like riches and a tiny piece of Israeli money.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel's currency unit is divided into one hundred smaller coins, each called by this name.

clue.text: Nearly led astray with erudition?

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of the two words before it wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone almost led off the right path, but in a scholarly manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarship, so acting with it is acting in a scholarly, well-read way.

clue.text: Insulate Bresnan to cause excitement?

annotationWithheld.why: Insulate Bresnan to cause excitement? (9): the only parse splits 'Insulate' as 'In' (container indicator) + SULATE (fodder) around TIM (Bresnan), so the one word does two jobs

clue.text: A body done in and left

indicators.note: the finished word is placed inside the body of people

parts.note: a band is a body of people, such as musicians
taken as written

explanation.surface: A corpse is murdered and dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done in' looks like one phrase meaning killed, but 'in' is the container signal and 'A body' gives A then a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been deserted or left behind.

clue.text: Thin slice of metal used in conflict

indicators.note: the metal is placed within the word for conflict

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A sliver of metal finds a use on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is any very thin flat piece, like a biscuit or a slice of silicon in electronics.

clue.text: Turn blows to find their direction?

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a key
socks are punches, blows

explanation.surface: Turning punches to learn which way they are coming from.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer names devices that show the direction of 'blows', meaning winds.
explanation.definitionFit: Airfield fabric cones swing to show which way the wind is coming from, so they help find its direction.

clue.text: Scramble as the change appears

indicators.note: change says the letters of the two words beside it are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A rush to grab something as coins appear in a till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scramble' looks like the anagram signal but is the definition; 'change' rearranges AS THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a hurried rush, which is what haste means as a noun.

clue.text: Warmonger — a little weed

parts.note: a hawk is a politician who favours war
a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: An aggressive politician dismissed as a bit of a weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawkbit is a yellow dandelion-like wild plant of lawns and meadows, commonly treated as a weed.

clue.text: "Heavy metals" drama detailed with the occasion of Caesar's end

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word for drama loses its last letter

parts.note: acting is performing drama
Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: A play about heavy-metal musicians, cut down and staged on the date Caesar died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means docking the tail, so the word for drama loses its last letter; 'with' links. The Ides of March is when Caesar was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: The actinide series of radioactive chemical elements, from actinium onward, are all heavy metals.

clue.text: Wandered off, but right away detained

indicators.note: read backwards from the answer: take the right letter away and what is left means detained

parts.note: stayed, as in a court order that held something back

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off but was promptly picked up and held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately'; it means take R from the answer to leave STAYED, 'detained', so the parse puts R into STAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from the proper path, so strayed means wandered off.

clue.text: Well dressed, it's concluded

definitions.meaning: warmly covered in plenty of clothes
a job finished and settled is said to be completed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both bundled up in warm clothing and brought to a neat close, as with a deal.

clue.text: In one's depression it could have stopped a lorry

definitions.text: In one's depression it could have stopped a lorry

indicators.note: could have means could hold, so the words that follow contain the answer

explanation.surface: Musing that, at a low moment, something might have brought a truck to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' sounds like low spirits but means pressing down: a foot brake does stop a lorry, the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing down the brake foot control is how a driver halts a heavy truck.

clue.text: Sat, having fought against having no work

indicators.note: having no work means the word for work is removed

parts.note: to oppose is to fight against
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone sat out, having resisted being left unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose is to sit for a portrait, so posed and sat match as past tenses.

clue.text: Weapon for a childless listener

parts.note: sp is the genealogical abbreviation for sine prole, Latin for without issue
the ear is the organ of hearing, a listener

explanation.surface: A weapon given to someone who has no children and likes to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole, 'without offspring') is used in family trees for someone who died childless.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long-shafted thrusting or throwing weapon with a pointed head.

clue.text: Cameron's "big idea" in Yorkshire, say?

parts.note: David Cameron promoted a political idea called the Big Society; put 'building' into it and you get the kind of mutual savings bank that the Yorkshire is an example of

explanation.surface: A UK prime minister's flagship policy being tried out in a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Building Society is a large British mutual lender; Cameron's 'Big Society' was his 2010 slogan for community action.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a mutual institution takes savers' deposits and lends mortgages; the Yorkshire is one example of the type.

clue.text: Square-cornered and confused

parts.note: a T-square is the drawing tool shaped like the letter
something with corners is angled

explanation.surface: A shape with right-angled corners that has somehow got muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangled mind or story is muddled and knotted, so it means mixed up.

clue.text: Out of service, having expired without suspicion

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, it puts the word for expired around the other piece

parts.note: to expire is to die
sus is British slang for suspicion, as in the old sus laws

explanation.surface: Someone died with no hint of foul play, and so is no longer working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. Sus is British slang for suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer used or in operation is out of service, like an abandoned railway line.
